selection.text:
Robustly Leveraging Prior Knowledge in Text Classification	Prior knowledge has been shown very useful to address many natural language processing tasks.

Many approaches have been proposed to formalise a variety of knowledge, however, whether the proposed approach is robust or sensitive to the knowledge supplied to the model has rarely been discussed.

A key problem arisen here, is how to leverage such knowledge to guide the learning process, an interesting problem for both NLP and machine learning communities.

First, to leverage prior knowledge to label data  ,  .

the balance among classes.

Related Work	There have been much work that incorporate prior knowledge into learning, and two related lines are surveyed here.

The other is to constrain the model directly with prior knowledge.

Andrzejewski et al.andrzejewski2011framework proposed a framework in which general domain knowledge can be easily incorporated into LDA.

There are also some active learning methods trying to use prior knowledge.

Conclusion and Discussions	This paper investigates into the problem of how to leverage prior knowledge robustly in learning models.

To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to address the robustness problem of leveraging knowledge, and may inspire other research.
